children: Whitehaven Coal's share price falls 2.1% to A$7.49 early, underperforming Australia's benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index, as investors focus more on port disruptions than a strong quarter operationally. Whitehaven reported 1Q equity sales of 6.0 million tons of coal. That missed Ord Minnett's expectations by 8% and reflected port disruptions in Queensland and New South Wales. "These temporary port disruptions at third-party infrastructure are outside management's control, but we would expect these to resolve over coming quarters," Ord Minnett says. Whitehaven's inventory built by 1.0 million tons in 1Q. Management expects this to unwind in 2Q, improving cash flow. "Overall, this is a strong quarter operationally, though we expect the temporary logistics impacts and increase in net debt to weigh on sentiment today," Ord Minnett says. (david.winning@wsj.com; @dwinningWSJ)
